metadata.note: The Hudson Valley Railway (incorporated 14 Aug 1901, operation ceased 12:01 a.m. 1 Dec 1928), the interurban and street railway system of the upper Hudson valley: Troy - Waterford - Mechanicville - Stillwater - Schuylerville - Fort Edward - Glens Falls, Glens Falls - Lake George - Warrensburg, Thomson - Greenwich, Mechanicville - Round Lake - Ballston Spa, Ballston Spa - Saratoga Springs, Saratoga Springs - Glens Falls, and the Saratoga Springs local lines; plus the four electric predecessors that ran under their own names before the consolidation (Stillwater and Mechanicville; Glens Falls, Sandy Hill and Fort Edward; Greenwich and Schuylerville; the Saratoga Electric / Union Electric / Saratoga Traction succession). Research report: research/branches/hudson_valley_railway.txt.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (ODbL), Overpass via maps.mail.ru, 2026-10-18, traced with opstrace.py (Workdir cache osmcache_hudson_valley_railway): ways carrying abandoned:name / name:railway / razed:name / name = 'Hudson Valley Railway' or 'Hudson valley Rwy', the OSM route relations 3550381 and 3643230 ('Hudson Valley Railway') and 1174327 ('Hudson Valley Saratoga Lake Line'), and the County Road 42 ways tagged old_railway_operator='Hudson Valley Railway'. None of the other HVR ways carries old_railway_operator, so the probe tagged them as the HVR's own for routing (cost 1x). Where the line ran in the street, named present-day streets were routed at 1.1x and are listed as inferred. OpenHistoricalMap was fetched for every lifted stretch and has no HVR ways; its unnamed rail there (the D&H Glens Falls branch and others) was down-weighted so the router could not take it. Fragment-to-fragment gaps up to 650 m were bridged straight (listed); longer gaps are declared straight joins. Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals; ot.spurs() empty for every feature.
metadata.operator_split: Pre-1901 predecessors are separate companies in their own colours, ending 1901; HVR features begin 1901 (or later). The Saratoga lines are split at the 30 Jun 1892 sale (Saratoga Electric -> Union Electric) and the 1896 foreclosure/acquisition (Union Electric -> Saratoga Traction). NOT split: the Dec 1906 United Traction Co. (D&H-controlled) purchase of a majority of HVR stock - cars, crews, timetables and every ERJ/PSC notice to 1928 stayed "Hudson Valley Railway" (CFC 1924; PSC 1917; L. F. Loree, D&H president, HVR president from 1907); HVR cars over UTC track into Troy and over D&H track Ballston - Saratoga (still HVR crews); the 1906 financial readjustment (securities only). The Warren County Ry (Glens Falls - Lake George, own name 11 Jul - 14 Aug 1901) is folded into the HVR feature, as the report recommends.
omitted: Albany through cars (HVR cars over UTC track Albany - Watervliet - Cohoes - Waterford): proven only for 1903 (Trolley Exploring) and 1915 (ERJ 3 Jul 1915) [ANCHOR] years; Albany - Watervliet would double-draw the UTC South Ferry - Troy feature. Omitted per the report and the tracing brief; mentioned here only.

Glens Falls city lines (South St and Knight St lines, the depot line and the belt line): only 1927 and 1928 are proven (ERJ 1927 vol 69; PSC approval of abandonment 12 Apr 1928, ERJ 1928 vol 71 pt 1), and no source names the streets they used. Drawing them would mean inventing the routes for a one-to-two-year span on a line that very likely ran for decades, so they are omitted until a route and a start year are sourced (the 1919 PSC decision on Glens Falls trolley wire and the "South Side line" is the obvious next source).

Saratoga Springs Belt line: first proven year 1922 [OPEN start], end 1925; its streets are not established (OSM relation 1174327 carries a loop via High Rock Ave, Excelsior Ave, East Ave and Maple Ave that may be it, unverified). Omitted rather than drawn on a guessed route.

South Glens Falls branch of the GFSH&FE before 1901: opening not established (report: NONE pre-1901). After 1903 its approach is shared with the HVR Saratoga - Glens Falls line; no separate local feature drawn.

Ballston Spa - Saratoga over the D&H third and fourth tracks (HVR cars c.1907 onward, jointly with the Schenectady Railway): end year not established, and the track is already drawn in cities/albany_commuter_rail.geojson - not double-drawn.
Pre-1901 operation of the Thomson - Fort Edward link (WC01 suggests 1900): builder/operator unknown, so 1900 cannot be coloured; drawn from 1901 under the HVR.
Saratoga Northern Railway: never ran an electric car (receivership 15 Jan 1900, RB01); its route became the HVR Saratoga - Glens Falls line in 1903. Not drawn.
Horsecar years, per Rule 5: Stillwater and Mechanicville 1 Jun 1883 - 25 Dec 1895; Glens Falls, Sandy Hill and Fort Edward 1885 - 1891.
metadata.existing_layer_note: No existing feature for the HVR or any predecessor before this layer (grep for Hudson Valley, Stillwater and Mechanicville, Sandy Hill, Greenwich and Schuylerville, Saratoga Traction, Union Electric, Saratoga Electric across data/: only prose mentions in dh_lake_george_branch.geojson, central_new_england_railway.geojson and amtrak.geojson). Overlaps by design: the HVR Troy - Waterford feature meets UTC utc-albany-troy (albany_troy_trolley.geojson) on Troy terminal streets only; the Glens Falls - Lake George feature runs beside, not on, the D&H Lake George branch (dh_lake_george_branch.geojson).

segments.note: Hudson Valley Railway cars and crews over United Traction Co. track from Troy (4th and Fulton Streets, near Union Station) through Lansingburgh to Waterford, where the HVR's own line began. The through-car contract with UTC is dated 7 Jun 1901 (ERJ 3 Jul 1915: the HVR "furnished at its own expense the men to run its cars over the tracks of the United Traction Company"), but the first CONFIRMED HVR car into Troy is May 1902 (Railroad Gazette 23 May 1902: "The southern terminus is now at Troy") - drawn from 1902; 1901 is a bracket not drawn. PSC 1915: "Extends from Waterford (trackage to center of city of Troy)". Ended with all HVR operation at 12:01 a.m. 1 Dec 1928 (D&H annual report for 1928; ERJ 1928 vol 72 lists "between Troy, Mechanicville and Stillwater" among the lines abandoned). Hourly in 1909 (TT09); the headway is sourced for 1909 only and is an estimate for other years. Rule 4: colour tracks who ran the trains (HVR crews), so this is HVR although UTC owned the track. Overlap: the UTC Albany - Troy feature (albany_troy_trolley.geojson) ends downtown, so the two meet only on Troy terminal streets. HVR through cars also ran Albany - Watervliet - Cohoes - Waterford over UTC track (proven 1903 and 1915 only); NOT drawn - see metadata.omitted.
sources: Segment-level: start 1902 from Railroad Gazette 23 May 1902 (first confirmed HVR car into Troy; UTC contract 7 Jun 1901 per ERJ 3 Jul 1915); end 1928 from the D&H 1928 annual report and ERJ 1928 vol 72; hourly headway from TT09 (1909 only); route of the street track not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 41.7 mi against 44 mi documented (TT09 mileposts from Troy: Waterford 4, Glens Falls 48), -5%. By section (traced vs documented): Waterford - Mechanicville 8.72 mi vs ~9 (TT09 4 -> 13); Mechanicville - Stillwater 2.61 vs ~3 (TT09 13 -> 16); Stillwater - Thomson 13.41 vs 14 (ERJ 1928 vol 71, "Stillwater - Northumberland 14 mi"); Thomson - Fort Edward 11.26 vs 11 (ERJ 1928 vol 71; TT09 30 -> 41); Fort Edward - Glens Falls 5.7 vs ~7 (TT09 41 -> 48). Waterford - Stillwater - Schuylerville - Thomson - Fort Edward (south edge) is on the OSM-mapped HVR grade: the side-of-road line OSM tags as railway=abandoned + name:railway='Hudson Valley Railway' on the US 4 / NY 32 (Hudson River Road, Hudson Ave, River Rd, Broad St) centreline, so those miles are drawn on the road centreline beside which the track ran (offset of the order of 10-20 m), and abandoned:name ways on the private-right-of-way stretches north of Coveville and between Thomson and Fort Edward. The Hudson crossing at Thomson is drawn where OSM maps the HVR's abandoned bridges (about 43.118-43.121 N); CFC 1924 says HVR cars used Greenwich & Johnsonville track at Thomson, and no G&J piece is drawn. APPROXIMATED: 15 straight gap bridges between mapped fragments, 1.63 mi in all, the longest 515 m, 306 m, 290 m, 274 m (the longest, 510 m, north of Fort Miller at about 43.228-43.232 N); no longer straight joins. STREET ROUTE INFERRED, about 6.3 mi: Fort Edward - Hudson Falls - Glens Falls is drawn on present-day US 4 (Broadway, Lower Main St, Main St) to Hudson Falls, then River St (NY 254), Lower Warren St and Warren St into Glens Falls to Centennial Circle (Glen and Warren Sts). No source names the streets; this is the old Sandy Hill road and the obvious trolley route, and the 1891-1928 track may have used other streets. The OpenHistoricalMap/OSM rail between Fort Edward and Glens Falls (the D&H Glens Falls branch) was deliberately not used.

segments.note: The Hudson Valley Railway main line, Waterford - Mechanicville - Stillwater - Schuylerville - Thomson - Fort Edward - Sandy Hill (Hudson Falls from 1910) - Glens Falls; through cars ran from Troy (see the Troy - Waterford feature). The HVR was incorporated 14 Aug 1901 (PSC 1915; McGraw Red Book 1901-02) as a consolidation of electric roads that already ran most of this route under their own names - the Stillwater and Mechanicville (Waterford - Mechanicville - Stillwater, electric 1895/1898), the Greenwich and Schuylerville (Stillwater - Schuylerville - Thomson, opened 1900) and the Glens Falls, Sandy Hill and Fort Edward (electric 1891) - each drawn as its own feature to 1901. The Thomson - Fort Edward link was open by July 1901 (Electrical Review 20 Jul 1901: Albany - Lake George "by trolley ... without break"); WC01 suggests 1900, but its builder/operator before the consolidation is not established, so it is drawn only from 1901 under the HVR. Not a change of operator: in Dec 1906 the United Traction Co. (itself controlled by the Delaware and Hudson) bought a majority of HVR stock (CFC 1924; PSC 1917), but cars, crews and timetables stayed "Hudson Valley Railway" to the end. The late-March 1913 flood interrupted through running (ERJ 5 Apr 1913) - an interruption, not an end. END: Stillwater - Schuylerville - Thomson - Fort Edward was abandoned effective 1 Jul 1928 (PSC approval 30 Apr 1928, ERJ 1928 vol 71 pt 2; last day 30 Jun 1928); Waterford - Stillwater and Fort Edward - Glens Falls ran until all HVR operation ceased at 12:01 a.m. 1 Dec 1928 (D&H 1928 annual report; ERJ 1928 vol 72), replaced by Hudson Transportation Co. buses. Both ends fall in 1928, so the whole feature is drawn to 1928. Hourly through cars Troy - Glens Falls in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only, an estimate for other years.
sources: Segment-level: start 1901 from the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation (PSC 1915; McGraw Red Book 1901-02) and Electrical Review 20 Jul 1901 for the Thomson - Fort Edward link; end 1928 from ERJ 1928 vol 71 pt 2 (Stillwater - Fort Edward, 1 Jul 1928) and the D&H 1928 annual report / ERJ 1928 vol 72 (rest, 1 Dec 1928); hourly headway from TT09 (1909 only).

segments.note: Glens Falls - Lake George (Caldwell; terminal at the Fort William Henry Hotel). Built by the Warren County Railway, which opened it on 11 Jul 1901 ("completed and cars were started on regular schedule July 11. The trip from Albany to Lake George by trolley can now be made without break" - Electrical Review 20 Jul 1901) and ran it for about five weeks under its own name before the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation into the HVR. Following the report, that five-week Warren County Ry operation is folded into this HVR feature rather than drawn as a one-year feature in its own colour. From 1922 lighter cars ran north of Glens Falls and through passengers changed there (secondary source, not independently checked). Ended 1 Dec 1928 (ERJ 1928 vol 72 lists "Lake George and Glens Falls" among the lines abandoned). Hourly Saratoga - Lake George - Warrensburg in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only, an estimate for other years.
sources: Segment-level: start 1901 from Electrical Review 20 Jul 1901 (opened 11 Jul 1901) and the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation; end 1928 from ERJ 1928 vol 72; hourly headway from TT09 (1909 only).

END: the HVR applied to abandon in Aug 1926 (ERJ 28 Aug 1926); the PSC denied it 8 Mar 1927 (ERJ 1927 vol 69) and later in 1927 authorised abandonment "between Lake George and Warrensburg" effective 31 Dec 1927 (ERJ 1928 vol 71 pt 1); Heritage Trail: service "through December 1927". Hourly Saratoga - Warrensburg, 35 mi in 1 h 50 min, in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only.

segments.note: Thomson - Clarks Mills - Middle Falls - Greenwich, along the Battenkill; connected at Greenwich with the steam Greenwich and Johnsonville. Opened 17 Jun 1900 by the Greenwich and Schuylerville Electric Railroad (drawn as its own feature to 1901); HVR from the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation. The HVR also switched G&J freight cars to mills on the branch - context only. END: the PSC approved (17 Aug 1927) a declaration of abandonment effective 1 Jan 1928, after denying the first application on 8 Mar 1927; a Battenkill flood washed out about 275 ft of roadbed near the American Woodboard Co. plant about 4 Nov 1927 and on 11 Nov 1927 the HVR asked to abandon "as of the date of the washout" (ERJ 1927 vol 70). Secondary sources put the washout in 1928; the ERJ dates it Nov 1927, so the line is drawn to 1927. Hourly from Thomson in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only.

segments.note: Mechanicville (Willow Glen trolley bridge, built 1902) - Coons Crossing - Round Lake - Kayaderosseras valley - Ballston Spa. Right of way still being secured in Aug 1901 (Electrical Review 24 Aug 1901); first CONFIRMED year 1902 (McGraw Red Book, Mar 1902: "branch lines to Mechanicsville, Round Lake, Ballston and Saratoga"; Railroad Gazette May 1902). END: petition heard 7 and 21 Oct 1925 (ERJ Oct 1925); PSC approval reported in the D&H report for 1925 (ERJ 1926 vol 67); ERJ 17 Jul 1926: the HVR "has abandoned ... the Mechanicsville-Ballston line, 13.67 miles long". Drawn to 1925, the last CONFIRMED operating year. This is NOT a known end - cars may have run into 1926 before the abandonment took effect, and no source dates the last car. Do not extend without evidence. Every 2 h Ballston - Round Lake - Mechanicville in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 6.0 mi against ~7 mi documented (inferred, not a stated figure), -14%. ALIGNMENT: this draws the ORIGINAL line (the Saratoga Traction Geysers line extended south), not the D&H third and fourth tracks that HVR and Schenectady Railway cars used jointly from about 1907 (RG08) - those D&H tracks are already drawn in cities/albany_commuter_rail.geojson and are deliberately not double-drawn. Drawn on the OSM relations 3643230 and 3550381 (Hudson Valley Railway): east side of Ballston Spa to the Milton pump station (about 43.015 N), then Avenue of the Pines and the abandoned way through the Spa State Park (the Geysers) to South Broadway. APPROXIMATED: one declared straight join of 3.43 mi from about 43.015 N to the Geysers (43.058 N, 73.802 W) - no HVR way is mapped there; the nearby OSM ways named 'Schenectady-Saratoga Trolley' / 'Railroad Run' / 'Old Ballston Avenue South' belong to the Schenectady Railway's line and were excluded; STREET ROUTE INFERRED, 0.73 mi: South Broadway / Broadway (US 9) to Congress St, the south side of Broadway where the report puts the Ballston cars' terminal; 2 straight gap bridges between mapped fragments, 0.12 mi in all, the longest 113 m, 80 m.

segments.note: Ballston Spa - the Geysers - Saratoga Springs (south side of Broadway; Glens Falls cars used a separate terminal on the north side - "passengers have to walk across Broadway", RG08). Opened under the Saratoga Traction Co. weeks before the consolidation (Electrical World 10 Aug 1901: "Saratoga and Ballston are now connected by the Saratoga Traction Company's lines"); per the report that 1901 Saratoga Traction anchor is folded into this HVR feature rather than drawn as a one-year feature. From about 1907 HVR cars also used the D&H's electrified third and fourth tracks jointly with the Schenectady Railway (RG08) - joint running, not a change of operator. END [OPEN]: passenger service on the old line is confirmed to 1911 by ERJ 15 Jul 1911 ("the old Hudson Valley Railway line now used between Saratoga and Ballston Junction might be abandoned"). This is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when HVR service on this line (or on the D&H tracks) actually stopped; it may have run to 1925/26, when the Mechanicville - Ballston line closed. Do not extend without evidence. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 1901 from Electrical World 10 Aug 1901 and the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation; end 1911 [OPEN] = last confirmed year, from ERJ 15 Jul 1911; joint use of D&H track from RG08. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 17.66 mi against 18 mi documented (SRJ03, "practically an air line"; 19 mi in TT09), -2%. MOSTLY APPROXIMATED: almost nothing of this line survives in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap. The only mapped trace is 'Trolleybed Lane' (0.08 mi, about 43.105 N, 73.770 W), used as an anchor. Straight-line legs: north Broadway, Saratoga Springs - Trolleybed Lane 1.74 mi; Trolleybed Lane - South Glens Falls (Saratoga Ave, US 9) 14.70 mi - 16.44 mi straight in all, 93% of the line. The source calls the line "practically an air line", so a chord is a fair approximation, but the real line followed the old Mount McGregor Railroad right of way as far as Wilton, which the chord does not show. STREET ROUTE INFERRED, 1.14 mi: Saratoga Ave (US 9) in South Glens Falls, the Cooper's Cave bridge (a modern bridge on the site of the river crossing - later-alignment caveat) and Glen St to Centennial Circle.

segments.note: Saratoga Springs (north side of Broadway) - Wilton - South Glens Falls - Hudson River bridge - Glens Falls, built under the North River Railway franchise (North River Ry incorporated 5 Apr 1902; stock bought by the HVR 1903 and leased to it 3 Jul 1903). Opened 1903 (SRJ 1903: "The Hudson Valley Railway Company opened its line from Saratoga to Glens Falls last week"; CFC 1924: "completed in June 1903") - the second route between the Capital District and Glens Falls. The Glens Falls - South Glens Falls bridge was carried away in the late-March 1913 flood, stopping through traffic (ERJ 5 Apr 1913) - an interruption, not an end. The South Glens Falls local (begun by the GFSH&FE c.1896, opening not established) shared this approach and ran to 1928. Ended 1 Dec 1928 (ERJ 1928 vol 72: "between Glens Falls and Saratoga"; bus fare 80c). Hourly, 50 min, in 1909 (TT09); headway sourced for 1909 only.
sources: Segment-level: start 1903 from SRJ 1903 and CFC 1924; end 1928 from ERJ 1928 vol 72 and the D&H 1928 annual report; hourly headway from TT09 (1909 only).

segments.note: Saratoga Springs (Broadway) - Saratoga Lake (Kaydeross Park, owned by the HVR), "a little over five miles". Electric since 1892 under the Union Electric Ry and then Saratoga Traction (drawn as their own features); HVR from the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation. Saratoga Traction ran it "only during the summer season" (RB01); whether the HVR ran it year-round is not known - seasonal service is still passenger service for the drawn year. END: in the same PSC proceeding as the Mechanicville - Ballston line (petition heard Oct 1925; approval reported in the D&H report for 1925; the PSC annual list in ERJ 1926 vol 68 names "the Kaydeross Park line ... extending from Saratoga Springs to Saratoga Lake"). Drawn to 1925, the last CONFIRMED year. This is not a known end - a 1926 summer season is possible and unproven. Do not extend without evidence. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 1901 from the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation (electric since 1892 per OCP99 and Electrical World 23 Jul 1892); end 1925 = last confirmed year, from ERJ Oct 1925, ERJ 1926 vol 67, ERJ 17 Jul 1926 and ERJ 1926 vol 68. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.

Built 1885 as a narrow-gauge horse road; "changed from horsepower to an electric road in 1891" (WC01). The railroad commissioners approved the change to electricity in 1891 (Street Railway Review vol 1); the earliest trade-press confirmation of electric operation in hand is Oct 1892 (Electrical World 1 Oct 1892, "superintendent, Glens Falls Electric Railway"). Drawn from 1891 on WC01 plus the 1891 approval; 1891 is less firm than 1892. Horsecar years 1885-1891 not drawn (Rule 5). Standard gauge by 1901 (RB01). A South Glens Falls branch (c.1896) is NOT drawn - its opening is not established. Consolidated into the Hudson Valley Railway 14 Aug 1901. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start 1891 from WC01 (Fort Edward gazetteer) and the 1891 commission approval (Street Railway Review vol 1), first trade-press confirmation Oct 1892 (Electrical World); end 1901 = the 14 Aug 1901 consolidation. Headway NOT sourced - estimate.
